camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates left around a fixed vertical axis without translating its position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: New space enters from the left while existing content exits right.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal or follow something located left of the current frame.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A frame with meaningful off-screen space to the left.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates right around a fixed vertical axis without translating its position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: New space enters from the right while existing content exits left.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal or follow something located right of the current frame.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A frame with meaningful off-screen space to the right.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates upward around a fixed horizontal axis without changing height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Lower content exits as higher parts of the subject or setting enter.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal height, a face, a tower or something above frame.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The opening frame must contain a lower visual anchor.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates downward around a fixed horizontal axis without changing height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Upper content exits as lower parts of the subject or setting enter.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal hands, feet, an object or something below frame.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The opening frame must contain an upper visual anchor.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates clockwise around the lens axis while remaining in position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The horizon continuously cants clockwise and the frame appears to spin.
camera_terms.use_when: Intensify vertigo, impact or psychological disturbance.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A readable horizon or vertical reference must be visible.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates counterclockwise around the lens axis while remaining in position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The horizon continuously cants counterclockwise and the frame appears to spin.
camera_terms.use_when: Reverse a prior roll or create rotational unease.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A readable horizon or vertical reference must be visible.

camera_terms.definition: The entire camera translates forward toward the subject, unlike a zoom which changes focal length from a fixed position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Perspective and parallax change as the subject grows and the background spreads outward.
camera_terms.use_when: Move the viewer physically closer to an important subject.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wider view with a clear path toward the subject.

camera_terms.definition: The entire camera translates backward away from the subject, unlike a zoom which changes focal length without translation.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Perspective and parallax change as the subject shrinks and more surroundings appear.
camera_terms.use_when: Withdraw emotionally or expose previously hidden context.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A close or medium view with safe space behind the camera.

camera_terms.definition: The entire camera translates left on a lateral path, unlike a dolly which travels toward or away from the subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground and background slide at different rates while framing shifts sideways.
camera_terms.use_when: Move alongside action or reveal around an obstruction.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A subject or reveal path extending left of the starting frame.

camera_terms.definition: The entire camera translates right on a lateral path, unlike a dolly which travels toward or away from the subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground and background slide at different rates while framing shifts sideways.
camera_terms.use_when: Move alongside action or reveal around an obstruction.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A subject or reveal path extending right of the starting frame.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rises vertically while its orientation and lateral position remain essentially unchanged.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewpoint gains height and lower foreground may clear without tilting.
camera_terms.use_when: See over an obstacle or raise the viewer to subject height.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A lower camera height with vertical clearance above.

camera_terms.definition: The camera descends vertically while its orientation and lateral position remain essentially unchanged.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewpoint lowers and foreground objects may begin to occlude the scene.
camera_terms.use_when: Drop to a child, seated subject or low story detail.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A raised viewpoint with vertical clearance below.

camera_terms.definition: A jib or crane arm raises the camera along an arc rather than a purely vertical pedestal line.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Height, distance and perspective change together as the camera sweeps upward.
camera_terms.use_when: Open a scene vertically or rise above subjects.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A low or medium start with clear overhead rig travel.

camera_terms.definition: A jib or crane arm lowers the camera along an arc rather than a purely vertical pedestal line.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Height, distance and perspective change together as the camera sweeps downward.
camera_terms.use_when: Descend into a scene or settle on a character.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A high start with a clear descending path.

camera_terms.definition: The lens changes focal length while the camera position stays fixed, unlike a dolly which translates and changes perspective.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The field of view narrows or widens without translation parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Change apparent magnification when physical movement is impossible or unwanted.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A stable frame with the target already visible near centre.

camera_terms.definition: The camera translates simultaneously along lateral and forward-or-back axes.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Subject scale and background parallax change along an oblique screen direction.
camera_terms.use_when: Approach while clearing an obstacle or changing the subject angle.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wide start with an unobstructed diagonal path.

camera_terms.definition: The camera travels through a partial curve around a subject while maintaining useful framing.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The background rotates behind the subject and profile changes progressively.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal relationships or move from one side of a subject to another.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A subject separated from obstacles with partial circular clearance.

camera_terms.definition: The camera travels around a subject through a broad circle, usually maintaining the subject near frame centre.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The entire environment revolves behind a relatively stable subject.
camera_terms.use_when: Celebrate, isolate or inspect a central subject.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred subject with full circular clearance.

camera_terms.definition: The camera orbits while simultaneously rising or descending around the subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The background rotates as camera height and subject angle change continuously.
camera_terms.use_when: Turn an orbit into an escalating reveal or descent.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred subject with circular and vertical clearance.

camera_terms.definition: The camera translates on a dolly while panning to redirect the optical axis.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Translation parallax combines with a changing horizontal view direction.
camera_terms.use_when: Pass a subject while keeping it framed or transfer attention.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide or medium frame with room for translation and rotation.

camera_terms.definition: The camera translates while tilting to maintain or change vertical framing.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Perspective changes while the view travels along the subject’s height.
camera_terms.use_when: Approach a tall subject and reveal upward or downward detail.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wide start on the lower part of a tall subject.

camera_terms.definition: The camera translates laterally while panning, usually to hold or pass a subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Strong parallax combines with an evolving front, profile or rear angle.
camera_terms.use_when: Track action while changing the viewer’s relation to it.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: truck sideways while panning on subject
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A visible subject with lateral travel space.

camera_terms.definition: The camera changes height while tilting to maintain or redirect framing.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewpoint rises or falls while vertical composition evolves independently.
camera_terms.use_when: Clear foreground objects while keeping a subject framed.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A subject already visible with vertical clearance.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rotates horizontally and vertically at the same time from a fixed support point.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame follows a diagonal or curved path across the scene without translation parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow airborne, climbing or diagonally moving action.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A subject positioned to travel diagonally across frame.

camera_terms.definition: A crane carries the camera through a large combined vertical and horizontal arc.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Scale, height, perspective and geography change in one continuous move.
camera_terms.use_when: Introduce crowds, architecture or landscape at production scale.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide spatial setup with a clear three-dimensional rig path.

camera_terms.definition: A short crane arm swings the camera laterally and vertically around its pivot.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The lens follows a compact curved path with noticeable foreground parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Add a controlled reveal in confined studio or location space.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A near foreground anchor and clear arm radius.

camera_terms.definition: The camera slides laterally while near and far elements remain at different depths.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground moves faster than background, making depth visibly separate.
camera_terms.use_when: Add depth to products, portraits, miniatures or landscapes.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: At least two visible elements must occupy distinct depth planes.

camera_terms.definition: A stationary tripod and fluid-damped head rotate the camera smoothly in pan or tilt.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Rotation is controlled and repeatable with no translation parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Make polished pans and tilts from a fixed position.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A stable support point and subject path within the head range.

camera_terms.definition: A wheeled platform carries the camera through space on track or a prepared floor.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Translation produces stable perspective change and controlled parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Execute precise pushes, pullbacks, tracking or compound moves.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A clear, level travel path and planned start mark.

camera_terms.definition: A camera carriage moves along a short rigid rail.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A compact linear translation creates controlled parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Add subtle motion to products, interviews or establishing details.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A composition with foreground and background separation.

camera_terms.definition: A pivoting counterweighted arm moves the camera through a compact vertical or lateral arc.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The view rises, falls or swings with smooth curved parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Create small crane-like moves where space or budget is limited.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: Clearance around the arm pivot and subject.

camera_terms.definition: A long counterweighted arm carries the camera through large vertical and horizontal arcs.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The shot can travel from intimate height to broad overhead geography.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal large sets, crowds, architecture or landscapes.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A broad unobstructed rig path and rehearsed end frame.

camera_terms.definition: A telescoping crane changes arm length while booming and swinging the remote camera head.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The lens can push, pull, rise and arc through complex three-dimensional paths.
camera_terms.use_when: Combine crane scale with a direct push-in or pullback.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide start with extensive overhead and forward clearance.

camera_terms.definition: A mechanically isolated body-worn stabilizer lets an operator walk or run with reduced shake.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The camera floats through space while retaining subtle human drift.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow characters through complex terrain without tracks.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A walkable route and subject position visible at the start.

camera_terms.definition: Motorized axes actively stabilize pan, tilt and roll while the operator or mount moves.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The horizon and orientation remain very smooth despite translation.
camera_terms.use_when: Create smooth low, high, vehicle or running moves.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A planned travel path with enough subject separation for tracking.

camera_terms.definition: The operator supports and aims the camera directly without a stabilizing platform.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Breathing, footfalls and grip corrections appear as organic frame movement.
camera_terms.use_when: Place the viewer inside documentary, conflict or intimate action.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The subject must be framed with margin for operator drift.

camera_terms.definition: The camera rests on the operator’s shoulder and moves with torso and steps.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The view has directional stability with characteristic vertical and rotational sway.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow action with more mass and control than bare handheld.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wider start with margin around the subject.

camera_terms.definition: A remotely piloted aircraft translates and changes altitude while carrying a stabilized camera.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewpoint crosses terrain freely at heights and paths unavailable to ground rigs.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal geography, follow vehicles or connect distant spaces.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide outdoor opening with safe aerial clearance.

camera_terms.definition: A remotely controlled camera carriage travels along tensioned cables above or through a venue.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The shot covers long repeatable aerial paths while remaining tied to the cable line.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow sport, concerts or crowds over long distances.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A broad venue view aligned with the cable route.

camera_terms.definition: The camera translates through space to maintain, approach or move alongside a subject, whereas following and leading specify positions behind or ahead.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Subject framing stays purposeful while environment and parallax evolve.
camera_terms.use_when: Accompany action while showing changing spatial context.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A visible moving subject and a clear travel direction.

camera_terms.definition: The camera travels behind or just off the rear of a moving subject, unlike generic tracking which can use any relative position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject leads into newly revealed space while the background approaches.
camera_terms.use_when: Let the viewer accompany a character into an environment.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A rear or rear-three-quarter view of a subject beginning to move away.

camera_terms.definition: The camera travels ahead of a moving subject while facing back toward them, unlike following from behind.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject advances toward camera as the background retreats behind them.
camera_terms.use_when: Show expression during forward travel.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: camera leads subject from the front
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A frontal medium or wide view with travel space behind the camera.

camera_terms.definition: The camera travels parallel to the subject from a side-on position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject remains in profile while the background scrolls laterally with strong parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Show locomotion clearly against changing surroundings.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A profile view and lateral route parallel to the subject.

camera_terms.definition: The camera aggressively follows one or more fast subjects while preserving directional continuity.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Rapid translation, corrections and changing gaps communicate pursuit.
camera_terms.use_when: Photograph running, driving or combat pursuit.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide rear or three-quarter view with open pursuit space.

camera_terms.definition: The camera tracks continuously with characters who converse while walking.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Dialogue framing persists as the environment flows past.
camera_terms.use_when: Deliver exposition without stopping the scene.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A two-shot or group framing with characters already walking.

camera_terms.definition: The camera travels while maintaining an over-the-shoulder relationship to a foreground character.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground shoulder overlap anchors viewpoint as the environment changes.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow a conversation, search or pursuit from a participant’s side.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A foreground shoulder and the tracked subject must both be visible.

camera_terms.definition: The camera moves as if occupying a character’s eyes or body position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Camera path and gaze changes directly represent the character’s locomotion.
camera_terms.use_when: Let the viewer experience walking, running, riding or searching first-hand.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A forward-facing view aligned with the implied character path.

camera_terms.definition: A rigid body-mounted camera faces the performer so camera and torso move together.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The face stays nearly fixed while the world lurches and rotates behind it.
camera_terms.use_when: Externalise disorientation while preserving facial performance.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A tight frontal view with the actor centred.

camera_terms.definition: A camera mounted on or operated from one moving vehicle tracks another vehicle or subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Speed is expressed through background flow while relative subject distance stays controllable.
camera_terms.use_when: Film driving, cycling or high-speed travel safely and consistently.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide or medium view of the target vehicle on a parallel route.

camera_terms.definition: An aerial camera travels above or behind a moving subject while adjusting position to retain it.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject remains readable within changing geography and altitude.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow people, animals, boats or vehicles across terrain.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide aerial view with the moving subject already identifiable.

camera_terms.definition: The camera path and orientation continually adjust so a chosen moving subject remains near a fixed frame position.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject appears compositionally stable while background motion carries most movement.
camera_terms.use_when: Keep erratic action readable or isolate one performer in motion.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The target must be clearly visible and separated from similar subjects.

camera_terms.definition: Action is recorded or generated with more temporal samples and played longer than real time, unlike a speed ramp which changes rate within the shot.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Movement stretches smoothly and small physical details become visible.
camera_terms.use_when: Emphasise emotion, athletic form, debris or a decisive instant.

camera_terms.definition: Action is played faster than real time at a constant rate, unlike a speed ramp which varies rate during the shot.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Travel and gestures compress into brisk, often comic movement.
camera_terms.use_when: Compress routine action or make a process feel frantic.

camera_terms.definition: Playback speed changes continuously or in stages within one shot, unlike constant slow motion or a frozen frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Motion accelerates or decelerates around a selected beat.
camera_terms.use_when: Enter slow motion for a key moment and return to real time.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The action must begin before the moment selected for the rate change.

camera_terms.definition: One image is held for a duration so all visual motion stops, unlike slow motion which still advances through time.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The moving shot becomes perfectly static before motion or editing resumes.
camera_terms.use_when: Punctuate an identity, impact, joke or turning point.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A clear decisive pose or readable action apex must be reached.

camera_terms.definition: Frames captured or generated at long intervals are played continuously to compress a long duration.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Slow processes such as clouds, traffic or construction move rapidly.
camera_terms.use_when: Show hours, days or gradual change within seconds.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A stable wide composition containing a visibly changing process.

camera_terms.definition: A time-lapse includes substantial controlled camera translation between recorded frames.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Long travel collapses into rapid forward movement with a relatively anchored target.
camera_terms.use_when: Compress movement through streets, buildings or landscapes.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred distant anchor and repeatable travel path are required.

camera_terms.definition: Selected intermediate frames are omitted so motion advances in discontinuous jumps.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Movement becomes choppy with abrupt spatial increments.
camera_terms.use_when: Create panic, malfunction or an intentionally broken cadence.

camera_terms.definition: Frames are optically or digitally repeated in groups while source action advances at a different cadence.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Moving subjects leave a smeared, pulsing or stuttering temporal trail.
camera_terms.use_when: Create expressive motion trails associated with stylised cinema.

camera_terms.definition: Each video frame uses a long exposure relative to frame duration so moving detail smears.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Subjects and camera movement produce flowing trails and reduced temporal crispness.
camera_terms.use_when: Suggest night energy, memory, dance or velocity.

camera_terms.definition: Each frame uses a short exposure so motion blur is reduced without changing playback speed.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Moving edges become crisp and action feels sharply segmented.
camera_terms.use_when: Make explosions, running or impacts feel immediate and abrasive.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The camera pans so rapidly that the image becomes directional blur, unlike an ordinary pan which preserves readable detail.
camera_terms.visual_effect: One scene smears horizontally into another across a hidden cut.
camera_terms.use_when: Connect locations, times or subjects with energetic direction.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A readable subject with open pan space toward the transition direction.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The camera tilts rapidly until vertical motion blur hides a cut to a matching tilt.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame streaks vertically and resolves into a new shot.
camera_terms.use_when: Change scenes using upward or downward visual momentum.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A frame with a clear vertical movement direction.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: A foreground object crosses the lens and progressively covers the frame to motivate a cut.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The moving occluder replaces one image area at a time with the next shot.
camera_terms.use_when: Hide a cut behind a passer-by, wall, vehicle or prop.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: An approaching foreground object must already be near one frame edge.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The camera moves into complete occlusion behind an object before cutting and emerging elsewhere.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The image darkens or fills completely, masking the edit.
camera_terms.use_when: Transition through doors, bodies, pillars or darkness.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A large nearby object must be able to cover the entire lens.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The camera pushes through an opening, surface or matched portal into a different scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame crosses a boundary and emerges in new space with forward momentum.
camera_terms.use_when: Link locations through doors, windows, screens or stylised surfaces.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred opening or surface large enough to fill the frame.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: A cut joins two shots whose camera direction, speed and framing continue one apparent movement.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The environment changes while camera momentum appears uninterrupted.
camera_terms.use_when: Link separate places or subjects without losing kinetic continuity.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The first shot must end on a reproducible motion vector and framing.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The edit occurs while the camera is actively moving so motion masks spatial discontinuity.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The cut feels softer because the frame is already changing.
camera_terms.use_when: Hide coverage changes inside pans, tilts or tracking moves.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The camera must already be moving decisively before the cut point.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The camera approaches a colour, texture or object until it fills the image before cutting to a matching field.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Recognisable space disappears into a full-frame visual surface and reopens elsewhere.
camera_terms.use_when: Match walls, clothing, darkness, light or texture between scenes.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A large target surface must be centred and reachable.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The moving camera is physically or virtually transferred between operators, rigs or spaces during one apparent take.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The shot continues through a change of support, height or access without a visible cut.
camera_terms.use_when: Move through windows, vehicles, stairs or impossible rig changes.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The camera must approach a reachable transfer point with stable framing.

camera_terms.category: Shot transitions and cuts driven by camera
camera_terms.definition: The moving camera passes behind a near vertical object that briefly fills the frame and conceals a cut.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Lateral parallax supplies a natural wipe into the next location.
camera_terms.use_when: Hide edits during tracking shots through architecture or crowds.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A near pillar, wall edge or person must intersect the travel path.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The lens zooms aggressively through a clearly visible brief interval, unlike a snap zoom which is nearly instantaneous and a dolly zoom which also moves the camera.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The field of view changes violently without translation parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Punch into or away from a sudden discovery.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wide view with the target already near the zoom centre.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The lens changes focal length almost instantaneously, faster and more jump-like than a crash zoom and without the camera translation of a dolly zoom.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Framing appears to jump rapidly to a tighter or wider scale.
camera_terms.use_when: Hit a reaction or detail with minimal transition time.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A clearly visible target must already occupy the zoom centre.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The lens changes focal length so slowly that the viewer may not consciously notice the reframing.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject gradually grows or recedes while perspective remains fixed.
camera_terms.use_when: Build attention or anxiety without obvious camera travel.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A stable medium or wide frame held long enough for gradual change.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The lens widens from a tight view to expose context without translating the camera.
camera_terms.visual_effect: More of the scene appears but perspective relationships remain fixed.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal that a detail belongs to a larger unexpected setting.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A tight opening on a detail that conceals the wider context.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The camera physically dollies backward from a tight view, producing parallax unlike a zoom-out reveal.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground and background separate as hidden surroundings enter frame.
camera_terms.use_when: Expose scale, danger, witnesses or geography around a subject.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: camera pulls back revealing full scene
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A close or medium opening that intentionally withholds context.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: A tilt begins on one part of a subject or setting and ends on previously off-screen vertical information.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The composition unfolds upward or downward without camera translation.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal height, identity, an object or a consequence.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The first frame must show a lower anchor while withholding the reveal above.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: A pan moves from an initial visual anchor to information hidden beyond a side edge.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame unfolds laterally and establishes a spatial relationship.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal another character, threat, landscape or punchline.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: The opening composition must withhold the reveal beyond one side.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: Focus transfers between depth planes to reveal a subject without changing camera position or framing size.
camera_terms.visual_effect: One plane sharpens as another softens, redirecting attention through depth.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal a background threat or transfer importance between characters.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: rack focus from foreground to background
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: Distinct foreground and background subjects must both be visible.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The camera moves laterally or vertically out from behind a near occluder.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A hidden subject or environment appears through changing foreground parallax.
camera_terms.use_when: Introduce a scene from concealment or add depth to an entrance.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: camera slides from behind foreground object
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A foreground object must initially conceal meaningful image area.

camera_terms.category: Framing that changes during the shot
camera_terms.definition: The operator pans, tilts or adjusts composition during the take in response to unexpected subject movement.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Headroom, lead room or subject placement visibly corrects as action changes.
camera_terms.use_when: Keep spontaneous performance readable without a rehearsed camera path.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wider frame with margin around the subject.

camera_terms.definition: The camera remains fixed to a rigid support with no intended movement for the duration.
camera_terms.visual_effect: All screen motion comes from subjects or environment while framing stays exact.
camera_terms.use_when: Contrast moving action with an immovable viewpoint.

camera_terms.definition: The operator handholds the camera while deliberately limiting shake and correction amplitude.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Small organic drift remains without losing readable composition.
camera_terms.use_when: Add life to dialogue or drama without chaotic motion.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wider frame with safety margin.

camera_terms.definition: The operator permits or adds large irregular handheld movement and rapid corrections.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The horizon, framing and subject position fluctuate visibly.
camera_terms.use_when: Place the viewer inside combat, disaster or psychological distress.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide enough opening to tolerate subject displacement.

camera_terms.definition: A shoulder-supported camera inherits the operator’s gait and torso rotation.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame has weighted vertical bounce and side-to-side rotational sway.
camera_terms.use_when: Give following footage physical mass and human cadence.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A medium or wide subject frame with travel margin.

camera_terms.definition: Mechanical stabilization isolates footfalls while allowing gradual operator-driven drift.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Translation feels smooth but not perfectly horizon-locked or robotic.
camera_terms.use_when: Move through architecture or crowds with a human floating quality.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A walkable route and planned subject distance.

camera_terms.definition: Motorized stabilization actively holds roll and often pan or tilt while the support moves.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The horizon stays unusually level and movement appears frictionless.
camera_terms.use_when: Create clean running, vehicle or orbit footage.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A visible horizon or strong vertical references.

camera_terms.definition: The frame wanders slowly through tiny unpatterned pan, tilt or translation changes.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A nominally static view feels gently alive rather than mechanically fixed.
camera_terms.use_when: Avoid sterile stillness in dialogue, memory or suspense.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A stable composition with room for slight edge movement.

camera_terms.definition: The image undergoes small rapid vibration around its intended framing.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Fine detail and edges tremble without large compositional displacement.
camera_terms.use_when: Suggest vibration, engine energy, impact or unstable mounting.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A sharp detailed frame where small vibration will be visible.

camera_terms.definition: A programmed motorized rig repeats an exact camera path, orientation and timing.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Movement appears geometrically smooth and precisely timed.
camera_terms.use_when: Create repeat passes, product shots, visual effects or exact transitions.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A marked start frame and unobstructed programmed path.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: The camera dollies while the lens zooms oppositely to preserve subject size, unlike a crash or snap zoom which does not translate the camera.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject stays stable while background perspective expands or compresses dramatically.
camera_terms.use_when: Visualise shock, spatial distortion or psychological rupture.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred medium view with clear foreground-to-background depth.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: An array or virtual camera viewpoint moves around action that is frozen or slowed far beyond normal camera capture.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Viewpoint changes substantially while subject time appears nearly stopped.
camera_terms.use_when: Inspect a decisive action from impossible temporal angles.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: bullet time orbit around frozen action
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A clearly posed action apex with open space around the subject.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: The performer and camera ride separate dollies moving together so the body appears to glide without walking.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject remains eerily fixed relative to camera while the environment slides past.
camera_terms.use_when: Externalise shock, resolve or altered consciousness.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A frontal or rear medium view with a straight travel path.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: A camera mounted at the front of a moving vehicle faces forward so the vehicle itself is absent.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Tracks or road rush directly toward the viewer from a machine-like viewpoint.
camera_terms.use_when: Create an early-cinema-style journey or driverless forward view.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A forward-facing wide view aligned with the travel route.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: A camera is driven rapidly on a low improvised or stabilized path to represent an attacking unseen force.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewpoint races close to the ground with aggressive obstacles and directional corrections.
camera_terms.use_when: Give an invisible entity a violent embodied point of view.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A low forward-facing wide view with a clear high-speed route.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: The camera makes a dramatic low-angle orbit around heroic subjects while the background carries large-scale action.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Subjects remain dominant as the world rotates and spectacle layers behind them.
camera_terms.use_when: Introduce action heroes, vehicles or triumphant teams.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred low-angle group or hero with circular clearance.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: A long Steadicam-style following move travels with characters through multiple connected spaces and background events.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Continuous geography, entrances and social hierarchy unfold without a cut.
camera_terms.use_when: Immerse viewers in a world through a choreographed arrival.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A rear three-quarter character view at the entrance to a connected route.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: The camera tracks centrally along a strongly symmetrical corridor, often following or leading a subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: One-point geometry streams toward or away from the viewer with controlled symmetry.
camera_terms.use_when: Turn architecture and forward motion into psychological pressure.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A centred corridor vanishing point with the subject on axis.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: A single flowing take uses camera movement and actor blocking to create changing compositions without visible cuts.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The shot repeatedly reframes relationships while preserving continuous time and space.
camera_terms.use_when: Stage dialogue or action whose emotional focus shifts organically.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: spielberg-style moving master in one take
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide or medium master frame with choreographed actor entrances and paths.

camera_terms.category: Named signature moves from film history
camera_terms.definition: A feature-length-style unbroken moving take passes through many spaces and encounters without editorial cuts.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Locations and time unfold as one continuous camera journey.
camera_terms.use_when: Create an ambitious uninterrupted passage through a world.
camera_terms.requires_start_framing: A wide entrance view leading into a fully choreographed multi-room route.

motion_terms.definition: The subject advances upright at a walking gait without an aerial phase.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Weight transfers heel-to-toe between alternating legs while opposite arms counter-swing and the torso advances steadily.

motion_terms.definition: The subject travels with repeated flight phases at a sustainable pace below an all-out sprint.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Each foot lands under the body, pushes off, and leaves both feet airborne briefly while bent arms counter-swing.

motion_terms.definition: The subject travels at near-maximum speed with forceful acceleration and long flight phases.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The torso leans forward, knees drive high, arms pump powerfully, and each forefoot strike propels a long rapid stride.

motion_terms.definition: The subject travels backward while the torso and gaze remain oriented generally forward.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Short backward steps land on the forefoot as the hips stay low and the arms balance or guard the body.

motion_terms.definition: The subject makes one or more lateral steps without fully turning the torso into the travel direction.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The lead foot moves sideways and the trailing foot closes or follows while the shoulders remain mostly forward.

motion_terms.definition: The subject moves continuously sideways while keeping the chest, gaze or weapon oriented toward a target.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The outside foot leads and the inside foot follows without crossing, keeping the hips low and upper body aimed.

motion_terms.definition: The subject travels along a curved path around another subject or fixed point.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Feet step tangentially around the centre while the torso and gaze often remain turned inward.

motion_terms.definition: The subject redirects travel from one path to another rather than continuing straight.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: A plant step absorbs momentum, the hips and shoulders rotate toward the new path, and the opposite leg drives away.

motion_terms.definition: The subject increases speed progressively from standing or walking into running.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The torso leans forward, step frequency and stride length increase, and arm drive grows over successive steps.

motion_terms.definition: The subject reduces forward speed progressively until becoming stationary.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Stride length shortens, the torso comes upright or leans back slightly, and several braking steps absorb remaining momentum.

motion_terms.definition: The subject drives a closed fist toward a target and retracts it to guard.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Force begins through the feet and hip rotation, travels through the shoulder, extends the elbow, lands through aligned knuckles, then recoils.

motion_terms.definition: The subject strikes a target with the foot or lower leg while balancing on the support leg.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The support foot plants and pivots, the striking knee chambers, the hip extends or rotates, and the leg retracts after contact.

motion_terms.definition: The subject places a limb or guard in the path of an incoming strike to stop or absorb it.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The body braces, the forearm or shin intercepts the attack, joints stay flexed, and weight shifts to dissipate force.

motion_terms.definition: The subject redirects an incoming attack away from its path rather than absorbing it as a block.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: A small timed hand, forearm or weapon movement contacts the attack obliquely and guides it past the body.

motion_terms.definition: The subject moves the body clear of an incoming attack without making a blocking contact.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The head, torso or feet shift off the attack line while balance stays loaded for recovery or counteraction.

motion_terms.definition: The subject jerks away from a strike, blast or sudden contact while remaining generally upright.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The contacted body part moves first, the torso follows, and limbs flare or tighten before balance is recovered.

motion_terms.definition: An external impact forces the subject rapidly backward beyond an ordinary recoil.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The torso snaps away, the feet lose or scramble for purchase, and the body travels backward before landing or recovering.

motion_terms.definition: Two subjects seize and control one another at close range through grips and body pressure.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Hands establish holds, hips lower, feet adjust for leverage, and each body pushes, pulls or turns against the other.

motion_terms.definition: The subject loses smooth gait and takes uncontrolled corrective steps without necessarily falling.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The centre of mass moves outside the support base, arms spread, and rapid uneven steps attempt to catch it.

motion_terms.definition: The subject’s foot is obstructed or misplaced and the body falls toward the ground.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Forward momentum continues as the caught foot stops, the torso pitches, hands reach out, and knees or body contact the ground.

motion_terms.definition: The subject loses postural support and sinks or drops largely in place.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Knees buckle, the spine folds or slackens, and body weight descends without a strong travel impulse.

motion_terms.definition: The subject transitions from lying or seated on the ground to standing.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Hands or one knee create support, hips lift, one foot plants, and the legs extend until balance returns upright.
motion_terms.prompt_fragment: pushing up from ground to stand

motion_terms.definition: The subject arrests an impending fall and returns the centre of mass over the feet.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Arms counter-swing, one or more recovery steps widen support, and the torso corrects opposite the original lean.

motion_terms.definition: The subject deliberately prepares the body to resist force or absorb an expected impact.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Feet widen and plant, knees and elbows flex, the core tightens, and arms guard or press against support.
motion_terms.prompt_fragment: planting feet and bracing for impact

motion_terms.definition: The subject rapidly lowers from standing into a compact crouched posture.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Knees and hips flex, the torso lowers between the legs, and hands adjust for balance or protection.

motion_terms.definition: The subject organises rhythmic full-body movement into expressive or choreographed patterns.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Weight shifts between feet while hips, torso, arms and head coordinate to a repeated rhythm and spatial phrase.

motion_terms.definition: The subject expresses success or joy through enlarged upward and outward movement.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Arms rise or spread, the torso lifts, steps bounce or jump, and the face opens into a smile or shout.

motion_terms.definition: The subject moves hands or arms deliberately to communicate meaning alongside or instead of speech.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: A hand leaves rest, traces a readable directional or symbolic shape, holds briefly, and returns or transitions.

motion_terms.definition: The subject makes a rapid involuntary protective reaction to a sudden stimulus.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Eyes blink, shoulders rise, the head retracts, and hands may lift before the body relaxes.

motion_terms.definition: The subject raises a hand and moves it repeatedly to signal greeting, farewell or attention.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The arm lifts, palm faces outward, and the wrist or forearm swings side to side several times.

motion_terms.definition: The subject dips and raises the head to signal agreement, recognition or encouragement.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The chin lowers through neck flexion and returns upward in one or more controlled cycles.

motion_terms.definition: The subject raises and releases the shoulders to signal uncertainty, indifference or helplessness.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Both shoulders lift toward the ears, elbows or palms may turn outward, and the shoulders settle.

motion_terms.definition: The subject rotates the head to redirect gaze while the torso remains mostly oriented elsewhere.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The eyes lead or follow neck rotation, the chin travels laterally, and the movement settles on a new eyeline.

motion_terms.definition: The subject performs an action at reduced speed with intentional control rather than temporal slow motion.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Acceleration stays gentle, pauses are readable, and each weight transfer finishes before the next begins.

motion_terms.definition: The subject initiates movement with a sudden high-force burst and rapid acceleration.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Muscles preload briefly, the body drives forcefully from the ground, and speed peaks almost immediately.

motion_terms.definition: The subject links actions continuously with smooth curves and minimal abrupt stopping.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Momentum transfers through joints in sequence so one gesture blends into the next.

motion_terms.definition: The subject begins, pauses and partially withdraws before committing to movement.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Weight shifts forward then back, limbs start incompletely, and short pauses interrupt progress.

motion_terms.definition: The subject’s continuing motion is visibly governed by existing speed and mass rather than fresh controlled steps.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The centre of mass travels beyond easy stopping, limbs trail or counterbalance, and recovery requires braking motion.

motion_terms.definition: The subject moves through abrupt uneven starts, stops and direction changes.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: Short muscle contractions produce discontinuous limb and torso positions with little smooth transition.

motion_terms.definition: The subject moves as though gravity and ground support exert little or no downward constraint.
motion_terms.body_mechanics: The body drifts from small pushes, limbs lag and rotate freely, and no footfall establishes weight.

notes: Researched against official documentation and production references from Google Veo, Adobe Firefly, Tiffen Steadicam, ARRI, Sony and the Academy. Reliability is a qualitative cross-model estimate as of 2026-08-11: simple pans, tilts, zooms, tracking and common body actions are generally more reliable than exact rig physics, multi-axis compounds, historical signatures or complex temporal effects. Disambiguation is embedded in the definitions: zoom changes focal length while dolly translates; truck moves laterally; whip pan is a blurred high-speed pan; tracking is position-agnostic while following trails and leading precedes; crash zoom is visibly aggressive, snap zoom nearly instantaneous, and dolly zoom combines opposing lens and camera movement; slow motion advances at a reduced constant rate, speed ramp varies rate, and freeze frame stops advancement. Sources: Google video prompt guide https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/video/video-gen-prompt-guide ; Adobe motion presets https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/mobile/work-with-audio-and-video/work-with-video/use-motion-presets-for-video-generation.html ; Adobe prompting guide https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-audio-and-video/work-with-video/writing-effective-text-prompts-for-video-generation.html ; Tiffen Steadicam history https://tiffen.com/pages/history-of-steadicam ; ARRI stabilizers https://www.arri.com/en/cine-systems/camera-stabilizer-systems/trinity-2-and-artemis-2 ; Sony PTZ cameras https://www.sony.com/ptz ; Academy technical database https://awardsdatabase.oscars.org/
